body.statement: Can the handle \(\mathfrak H^{\mathrm{low}}\) exhibit constants \(\eta\in(0,1-2\alpha)\), \(\varepsilon_R\in(0,\min\{R_f,R_q\})\), and \(c_{\mathrm{sep}}>0\), and construct \(P_{0,n},P_{1,n}\in\mathcal M\) for all sufficiently large \(n\), with fixed \(p_x\), fixed positive \(f_x\), and fixed nonidentical asymmetric laws of \(U_1,U_2\) shared across \(j\in\{0,1\}\) and across \(n\), such that only the Bernoulli conditional means \(b_{j,n,x}\) differ; \(1/4\le b_{j,n,x}(a)\le3/4\) for every \(a\in\mathcal A\); \(\sup_x\|f_x\|_{H^{\beta}}\le R_f-\varepsilon_R\) and \(\max_{j\in\{0,1\}}\sup_x\|f_xb_{j,n,x}\|_{H^{\beta}}\le R_q-\varepsilon_R\); \(\operatorname{TV}(((P_{0,n})_{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n},((P_{1,n})_{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n})\le\eta\); and \(\|\mu_{1,n}-\mu_{0,n}\|_{L^{\infty}(I)}\ge c_{\mathrm{sep}}K_n^{1/2-\beta}\)?
body.justification: This fixed-nuisance Bernoulli modulus is the lower-bound headline: it isolates the genuinely new statistical obstruction before any generic confidence-band reduction is invoked.
body.gap: Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Lehéricy perturb the latent density and separate in \(L^2\); no comparator fixes the density and both asymmetric error laws while producing a valid Bernoulli marked perturbation with \(K_n^{1/2-\beta}\) supremum separation and an explicit \(\eta<1-2\alpha\) contiguity bound.
body.consumer: An affirmative construction supplies the sharp local experiment needed to certify the resolution limit of every honest two-recall ADRF band.

obligation.what_is_open: Construction of the fixed-nuisance Bernoulli packet and its product-experiment total-variation bound remains open after the analytic attenuation calculation.
obligation.obstruction: The declared index ranges do not even ensure a nonempty strict-interior lower submodel: they omit \(\kappa|I|\le1\), the necessary Sobolev-radius lower bound, and an interior spectral restriction excluding \(c_0=1\) for asymmetric errors. Under compatible indices, the missing mathematical step is a weighted chi-square or Hellinger bound for the two-replicate baseline together with a packet satisfying all range and Sobolev constraints.
obligation.attempted: I carried the moment-annihilation packet through the exact marked-channel Fourier factorization and obtained factorial low-frequency attenuation. I also tested the frozen index endpoints and found explicit feasibility obstructions before the total-variation conversion.
obligation.partial_result:
Two necessary compatibility checks follow from the frozen assumptions.  Every candidate fixed density must satisfy
\[
 1=\int_{\mathcal A}f_x(a)\,da\ge\int_I f_x(a)\,da\ge\kappa |I|
\]
and, by Cauchy--Schwarz and \(|\mathcal A|=2B_A\),
\[
 R_f\ge\|f_x\|_{H^\beta}\ge\|f_x\|_2\ge(2B_A)^{-1/2}.
\]
Neither restriction is imposed on the declared index ranges.  There is also an error-law obstruction at the allowed endpoint \(c_0=1\): if a characteristic function obeys \(|\phi(t)|=1\) on a nondegenerate interval, equality in \(|E e^{itU}|\le1\), at two noncommensurate nonzero frequencies, forces \(U\) to be almost surely constant.  Thus the required asymmetric compact-spectrum errors cannot exist at that endpoint.

Conditional on compatible fixed nuisances, the proposed polynomial-packet route does have the required analytic attenuation.  If \(h_n=f(b_{1,n}-b_{0,n})\) annihilates all polynomials of degree below \(K_n\), then for \(|u|\le\Omega\), Taylor's formula gives
\[
 |\widehat h_n(u)|
 \le \|h_n\|_1 e^{B_A\Omega}\frac{(B_A\Omega)^{K_n}}{K_n!}.
\]
For errors whose transforms are supported in fixed intervals, the two-dimensional Fourier transform of the marked observed-density perturbation is exactly
\[
 \widehat h_n(s+t)\phi_1(s)\phi_2(t),
\]
so it is confined to a fixed square and has the same factorial attenuation.  What remains is to construct the packet with the simultaneous \(H^\beta\), Bernoulli-range, and \(L^\infty(I)\) calibrations and to convert this Fourier bound into a uniform product-experiment total-variation bound through a proved lower envelope for the baseline observed density.
